title: Improving Adversarial Data Collection by Supporting Annotators: Lessons from GAHD, a German Hate Speech Dataset

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating hate speech detection models (fine-tuned PLMs, LLMs, and commercial APIs) on adversarial examples targeting racial and ethnic groups (e.g., Black people, Asians, Africans) using macro F1 scores, functional tests (HateCheck), and error analysis to identify false positives and false negatives.

Testing model robustness against adversarial texts containing xenophobic hate speech, non-hateful stereotypes, and counter-speech regarding migrants, refugees, and specific nationalities (e.g., Turkish, Pakistani, Polish, former Yugoslavians) collected via dynamic adversarial data collection (DADC).
Assessing the classification accuracy and error rates of models on dynamic adversarial data containing anti-Semitic content and Islamophobic rhetoric or neutral discussions about Muslims.

Benchmarking content moderation APIs and language models on adversarial examples discussing gender roles and women's rights to measure robustness against sexism-related hate speech and over-flagging of neutral text.

bias_targets.target: Sexual orientation and Gender Identity bias
bias_targets.methodology: Analyzing the performance of target models on texts specifically targeting LGBTQ+ rights, transgender, and intersex individuals within the German Adversarial Hate speech Dataset (GAHD).
Evaluating model detection capabilities on ableist hate speech and complex non-hateful references to disabled individuals using manually crafted and contrastive adversarial examples.

Measuring model robustness on adversarial examples explicitly targeting poor people, based on the dataset's expanded definition of protected groups, to see if models correctly identify classist abusive language as hate speech.
